For 1<=t<n, shared colors lie only at unmatched positions; at t=1 prohibit n-1 shared colors because the cross matched endpoints then have equal neighborhood color sets. With t=n, at most one reused color with different indices; t=0 has true twins. Choosing paired shared colors and injective fresh colors yields each falling-factorial summand, including n=2,t=2 boundary. Independently checked 62 (n,t,k) instances against the ORIGINAL graph/neighborhood definition for n=2..4; not an infinite computational proof.
